summary: Claude Code invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming on the ambiguous "add a userId parameter" brief, asked clarifying questions, explicitly upgraded the task to the architectural path after my minimal answers, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for approval, and only began implementation planning after I approved. No implementation code was written before approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are supported by directly observed screen text, session-log greps, and on-disk files. The router escalated to architectural, produced a spec document at the expected path, surfaced it for approval, and held off on implementation until approved.

observations.description: Codex companion spec review degraded silently: 'the Codex companion is installed and preflight passed (version 0.0.0-stub), but the spec review call returned an empty response, so the spec was not independently reviewed by Codex.' The agent recorded a ledger entry (20260917T100302Z-19565-28463) and proceeded. Worth investigating why the stub returned empty.

The agent initially presented a 4-option question whose recommended answer ('Caller already has it ... Stays bounded, ~3 lines') nudges toward the bounded path; only my clarification about cross-app persistence triggered escalation. A less-forthcoming human could easily land on bounded.
Multi-select question ('tooling') has no obvious affordance that Submit is a separate row below the options; I had to arrow past 'Type something' to find it.

The agent created a .gitignore excluding docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers citing a 'standing preference' I never expressed — spec docs therefore never get committed, which conflicts with criterion language about a 'committed spec file'.
Final design contradicts the literal user request ('No userId parameter is added anywhere'). The agent flagged this clearly, which is good, but it is a notable scope inversion.
Two separate approval gates ('approve design' then 'approve spec') required the same 'looks good, go ahead' twice; could be confusing about what is being approved.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming","args":"Add a userId parameter to the login function to track who logged in"}'

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote a spec doc to docs/{super,hyper}powers/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Log line: 'That answer changes the classification. **I'm upgrading this to the architectural path** — I'll stop and design before any code.' Spec file exists: coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-store-design.md, header '# User Identity Store — Design ... Status: approved for planning'

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-store-design.md (not committed)... Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan.' and 'no implementation code exists yet'. `git status --short` in workdir showed only '?? .gitignore' — no source edits.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly upgraded off the bounded option after clarification ('I'm upgrading this to the architectural path'); a spec file was committed to disk at docs/hyperpowers/specs/ rather than an in-chat-only design.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe plan appeared; the agent ran questions → approaches → sectioned design → spec → plan ('Spec approved. Moving to the implementation plan.' then Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)).
